meta.name: break-detection gold set
meta.purpose: Frozen, hand-labelled regression set gating any change to the reconcile prompt or extractor model. Scored by scripts/score_gold_set.py.
meta.seeded_from: 2026-08-29 replay of 90 archived briefs; seed artifacts live at from-server/replay-2026-08-29/ (gitignored, local only).
meta.seed_prompt: replay.py TEMPLATE - carries the absence guard but NOT the restatement guard, so these detections predate the guard now live in brief_memory._RECONCILE_TEMPLATE.
meta.labeller: single annotator, rationale recorded on every row; not independently reviewed. Disagree with a label by editing it - the rationale is there to be argued with.

labels.true_break: The later text contradicts, reverses or reports the claim as no longer true.
labels.false_break: The later text restates, escalates, confirms or is merely adjacent. Marking it broken is a false positive.
labels.unclear: Not decidable from the two texts alone. Excluded from the precision denominator and reported separately.

meta.admissible: Whether the claim should have entered the ledger as a durable fact at all. false marks the ephemeral-price admission failures the claim-admission guard (news-brief-93u) must reject upstream. Independent of label.

excluded_rows.reason: Claim and broken_by both carry Bigdata.com-derived numeric values (media pressure / attention scores). This repo is public and the enrichment integration is scoped to a derived-only snapshot, so the row is kept local rather than committed. It is an ephemeral-price admission failure, not a break-detection case, so the break set loses no coverage.

baseline.recorded_in_spec: ~61% precision (about 11 of 18 clearly classifiable), spec section 12.1
baseline.this_labelling: computed by scripts/score_gold_set.py from the labels below
baseline.note: The spec figure came from an in-session eyeball over audit.py output, which prints claim[:105] of a field replay.py had already truncated to 150 chars. These labels were made against the untruncated checkpoint text and disagree with it. Treat the labels here as the baseline of record; the ~61% is not reproducible.

meta.gate: The restatement guard must convert the false_break rows without losing the true_break rows. A run that improves recall while dropping precision below this baseline is a regression, not progress. n is small - read the per-item table, not only the aggregate.

items.claim: Iran suspended talks after Israel escalated Lebanon offensive; no MOU signed. IRGC threatens full Hormuz closure and Bab al-Mandeb activation.
items.broken_by: Iran abruptly suspended peace discussions and threatened full Hormuz closure in retaliation for ceasefire violations triggered by Israeli Lebanon escalation
items.label: false_break
items.rationale: Same suspension event restated with the Lebanon trigger spelled out. Nothing in the later text negates the claim.

items.claim: Iran threatened to activate Bab al-Mandeb, making Red Sea/Suez traffic comparable to Hormuz disruption if escalation continues.
items.broken_by: Quds Force commander Ghaani escalated threat to include Bab al-Mandeb closure, compounding Hormuz disruption across multiple chokepoints
items.label: false_break
items.rationale: Adds the attribution (Ghaani) and the word 'escalated' to a threat the claim already records. Escalation of wording is not contradiction.

items.claim: Brent near $90 while US equities at record highs—two competing narratives that cannot both be right for long absent Iran deal.
items.broken_by: Brent at $95.78 (+2.8%) Sunday open following Iran missile strike on Israel; oil rallying sharply on escalation.
items.label: unclear
items.rationale: The claim welds a durable thesis ('two narratives cannot both be right') to an ephemeral price anchor ('Brent near $90'). Brent at $95.78 supersedes the anchor while arguably confirming the thesis; which half is 'the claim' is not decidable from the text.

items.claim: Romania invoked Article 4 after drone strike; NATO focus remains on strengthening eastern flank defences via Article 4 consultations rather than Article 5.
items.broken_by: Romania did not ultimately initiate Article 4 consultations after the June 5 Ukrainian drone detonation; instead demanded accelerated air-defence equipment delivery.
items.label: true_break
items.rationale: Direct negation of the operative verb: 'Romania invoked Article 4' against 'Romania did not ultimately initiate Article 4 consultations'.

items.claim: BOJ raised policy rate to 1.0% on June 16; highest since 1995. Inflation pressure and yen stability drove tightening decision.
items.broken_by: BOJ rate decision executed at 1.0%, not just expected
items.label: false_break
items.rationale: The canonical false positive (spec 12.1). 'Executed at 1.0%, not just expected' asserts the same rate at stronger modality.

items.claim: US–Iran MOU signed June 14; 60-day negotiation window agreed but now functionally suspended after three consecutive nights of kinetic exchange.
items.broken_by: MOU in free fall; ceasefire has produced three consecutive nights of kinetic exchange; IRGC launched ballistic missiles and drones at US bases in Kuwait and Bahrain early Sunday.
items.label: false_break
items.rationale: The claim already states the MOU is 'functionally suspended after three consecutive nights of kinetic exchange'. The later text repeats that and adds detail.

items.claim: US and Iran reached agreement to end fighting and reopen Strait of Hormuz; formal signing scheduled June 19 in Switzerland.
items.broken_by: Trump declared the deal 'now complete' with signing scheduled June 19, contradicting prior 24-hour timeline and Sunday signing claims.
items.label: false_break
items.rationale: 'Deal now complete, signing June 19' confirms the claim. The word 'contradicting' in the later text points at a different prior timeline, not at this claim.

items.claim: Portugal defeated Uzbekistan 5–0 in World Cup Group K play; Portugal tops group with 4 pts (GD+4) heading into final matchday vs Colombia June 27.
items.broken_by: Both Colombia (4 pts) and Portugal (4 pts) are tied going into today's match; neither has secured group top yet. Portugal can secure top with win or draw.
items.label: true_break
items.rationale: 'Portugal tops group' is negated by 'both on 4 pts, neither has secured group top yet'.

items.claim: Colombia vs Portugal Group K final matchday June 27 is effectively a knockout; Colombia holds 6 pts, Portugal 4 pts on goal differential.
items.broken_by: Both Colombia and Portugal are on 4 pts; Colombia does not hold 6 pts.
items.label: true_break
items.rationale: Explicit numeric negation: 'Colombia holds 6 pts' against 'Colombia does not hold 6 pts'.

items.claim: Iranian negotiator confirmed Tehran intends to resume collecting fees from Hormuz-transiting vessels once 60-day suspension expires.
items.broken_by: Trump reversed course on the Hormuz toll — the 20% cargo fee is now being replaced by Gulf state investment deals in the US
items.label: true_break
items.rationale: Tehran's stated intent to resume collecting Hormuz transit fees is reversed by the toll being replaced with Gulf investment deals.

items.claim: Oman outlined plan for shipping companies to pay service fees transiting Strait, mirroring Malacca model, hardening structural tolling dispute.
items.broken_by: Trump reversed course on the Hormuz toll — the 20% cargo fee is now being replaced by Gulf state investment deals in the US
items.label: unclear
items.rationale: Oman's service-fee plan and Trump's 20% cargo toll are plausibly distinct instruments; reversing the latter does not clearly kill the former. Same broken_by as r-0493, where the link is direct.

items.claim: Chip names round-tripped: MU -10.4%, SKHY -10.2%, TSM -3.7% erase yesterday's capitulation bounce; positioning now purely momentum-driven, not fundamentals-driven.
items.broken_by: Today's whipsaw reversal shows no new information beneath; CXMT Shanghai debut and AI-capex doubt remain same overhang; momentum trading confirmed.
items.label: false_break
items.rationale: The claim asserts positioning is 'purely momentum-driven'; the later text ends 'momentum trading confirmed'. It confirms the thesis. The claim is also a one-day price move and should not have been stored.

items.claim: Japan's 10-year government bond yield held around 2.88% on Thursday, near highest level in almost three decades as Iran-US conflict drove oil prices higher.
items.broken_by: Japan's 10-year JGB yield has pulled back to ~2.70% from last week's 2.90% high after Finance Minister Katayama's remarks on steering pension money toward domestic assets.
items.label: false_break
items.rationale: The spec's named admission failure. A dated observation ('held around 2.88% on Thursday') is not contradicted by a later different level; the yield moved, the claim did not become false.

items.claim: Brent oil surged 1.2% on Sunday, first real repricing of Gulf-wide escalation after days of muted reaction to ceasefire breakdown.
items.broken_by: Brent is muted at +0.1% today; market is pricing 'contained war' not 'closed strait' and repricing trigger is Iranian tanker hit, not base strikes.
items.label: true_break
items.rationale: The thesis 'first real repricing has begun' is negated by 'Brent muted at +0.1%, repricing trigger is the Iranian tanker hit, not base strikes'. A real break, but on a claim anchored to one day's move.

items.claim: SK Hynix +13% overnight confirms memory-AI bull case reasserting post-selloff; MU's lag is divergence to watch, not confirmation of memory thesis.
items.broken_by: MU -7.4% and SKHY -3.0% today are giving back the memory-complex bounce; memory-AI bull case needs TSMC's print this afternoon to hold.
items.label: true_break
items.rationale: 'Memory-AI bull case reasserting' is negated by 'giving back the bounce; the bull case needs TSMC's print to hold'. A real reversal of the stated thesis, resting on overnight moves it should not have been built on.

items.claim: Brent muted at -0.2% today despite escalating multi-front strikes; market pricing 'contained war' not 'closed strait'—repricing trigger remains Iranian tanker hit.
items.broken_by: Brent +3.8% on seventh consecutive night of US strikes and Iran's tanker mine claims; repricing trigger has now fired.
items.label: true_break
items.rationale: The claim names its own falsifier ('repricing trigger remains the Iranian tanker hit'); the later text reports that trigger firing. A well-formed conditional thesis, correctly broken.

items.claim: Iran has no plans for negotiations and remains focused on defending the country; FM spokesman Baghaei stated Iran currently has no negotiations with US.
items.broken_by: Trump declared the ceasefire 'over' and CENTCOM began retaliatory strikes Wednesday night, indicating resumed active military operations contradicting any standing diplomatic posture.
items.label: false_break
items.rationale: The claim is about the absence of negotiations. Resumed CENTCOM strikes are consistent with it, not contrary to it. The later text asserts a contradiction it does not establish.

items.claim: Trump re-linked Saudi nuclear deal to Israel recognition; Riyadh must normalize before pact takes effect, re-hardening Abraham Accords expansion constraint.
items.broken_by: Trump administration explicitly says Saudi nuclear pact will only go into effect if kingdom normalizes with Israel, reversing earlier quiet delinking.
items.label: false_break
items.rationale: Near-verbatim restatement of the same re-linking, with 'reversing earlier quiet delinking' describing the world before the claim, not after it.

items.claim: Trump cancelled planned harshest bombing campaign against Iranian energy infrastructure after Saudi Crown Prince MBS called to caution him; deal framework contingent on Hormuz opening and Iran nuclear halt.
items.broken_by: Trump says he agreed to cancel the attack on Iran's energy infrastructure after Tehran and Gulf states asked for pause, citing deal framework
items.label: false_break
items.rationale: Same cancellation, same deal framework; only the attributed prompt differs (MBS vs Tehran and Gulf states). A differing detail is not a reversal.

items.claim: Trump reversed course on imminent Iran strike, agreeing to cancellation contingent on Hormuz strait opening and end to Iran nuclear threat.
items.broken_by: Trump says he agreed to cancel the attack on Iran's energy infrastructure
items.label: false_break
items.rationale: Strictly less specific restatement of the same cancellation. Near-duplicate of r-0775, which is itself a dedup failure.

items.claim: RGLD -0.6% while Barrick (GOLD) +1.1% and bullion flat; unusual split given RGLD's negative sentiment, volume spike yesterday worth monitoring into Nov 5 earnings.
items.broken_by: Today shows RGLD +1.6% and gold +1.4% moving together; bullion-miner divergence has closed.
items.label: false_break
items.rationale: A one-day divergence observation followed by a different one-day observation. The claim was never durable, so nothing about it was broken.

items.claim: Over 80% of Hormuz liquids traffic now routes via Oman; Iran losing physical control of strait despite escalatory rhetoric.
items.broken_by: CNN reports Iran is losing the Hormuz battle; more than 80% of liquids transits now run the Omani route Iran opposes, material shift from kinetic equilibrium framing.
items.label: false_break
items.rationale: The spec's second named false positive. 'More than 80% of liquids transits run the Omani route' restates 'over 80% of Hormuz liquids traffic now routes via Oman'.

items.claim: Bessent's Iran sanctions reveal excluded Chinese banks; Treasury deferred pressure ahead of Xi-Trump summit rather than escalating into it.
items.broken_by: Treasury did not include Chinese financial institutions in sanctions list; Bessent deferred naming facilitators ahead of summit
items.label: false_break
items.rationale: 'Treasury did not include Chinese financial institutions' restates 'Bessent's sanctions excluded Chinese banks'. Same fact, same direction.
